title: 8 משחקים וספרים שיעזרו להם לפצח חידות

stage.need: Problem solving around ages 6 to 8. KidsHealth, Smart Toys for Every Age: 'Jigsaw puzzles help with coordination and dexterity, and teach about spatial relationships (where things are in relation to other things) and logical thinking' and 'board games like checkers or chess teach about strategy, turn-taking, negotiating rules, and fair play'. Puzzle games give a small problem with a way to check the answer, activity books give mazes and puzzle pages to work through at the child's own pace.
stage.age_caveat: Ages are approximate: the sources describe play in general, not an age limit. Some 6 year olds already plan several moves and some 8 year olds still need a hint; the frame says בסביבות and the caption says יש ילדים ש....

dev_sources.title: Smart Toys for Every Age
dev_sources.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (medically reviewed by Elana Pearl Ben-Joseph, MD; date reviewed June 2018)
dev_sources.quote: Puzzles. Jigsaw puzzles help with coordination and dexterity, and teach about spatial relationships (where things are in relation to other things) and logical thinking. / Card and board games. Card games like "war" or "crazy eights" and board games like checkers or chess teach about strategy, turn-taking, negotiating rules, and fair play. / Blocks and construction sets. Building a tower (and figuring out how to stop it from toppling over) encourages problem-solving skills and hand–eye coordination. / Arts and crafts. As fine motor skills improve, activities like holding a crayon, drawing pictures of family members, and using a pair of safety scissors to cut and paste strengthen coordination, encourage creativity, and foster self-esteem.
dev_sources.supports: Puzzles teach spatial relationships and logical thinking; board games teach strategy and fair play; construction play and crafts exercise problem solving, hand-eye coordination and fine motor skills. Preschool and school-age play in general, not these products. Read through a page fetch; sentences joined with ' / '.

notes: Weekly batch 2026-10-18, slot 7, first carousel (assigned skill problem_solving, ages 6 to 8, format mixed). 8 suggestions: 4 games, 3 books and the LumeBook book, order game, book, game, book, game, book, LumeBook, game. All Israeli evidence read on 16 Oct 2026. Rush Hour Junior is available_in_israel only (thin evidence); one book (the school readiness workbook) is only partly about puzzles (low confidence). Images are retailer packshots, rights_unverified. The one dev source (KidsHealth Smart Toys for Every Age, 2018) is about play in general: no official page was found that states a 6 to 8 problem solving milestone and could be read today.
